record.original_question: What mathematically adequate genotype-to-phenotype maps are needed to explain how genes, gene expression, and their interactions produce phenotypes and complex diseases, especially when evolutionary dynamics combine deterministic selection, stochastic effects, and potentially omnigenic inheritance?

evidence.quote: The upshot of the wealth of data, and the complicated interplay between deterministic and stochastic effects in driving evolution, is that we need more sophisticated maps from genotype to phenotype, especially if the view of omnigenic inheritance persists [73, 74, 75].

Having better understanding of how genes, their expression, and their interactions affect phenotypes may help in resolving long standing questions in both fundamental biology, but also in understanding the causes and mechanisms of complex diseases.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a mathematically rigorous framework for genotype-to-phenotype (GP) maps with the following requirements. Let $G$ denote a space of genotypes (e.g., sequences over a finite alphabet, or vectors of allele states across many loci), let $E$ denote an environment space, and let $P$ denote a phenotype space (which may be high-dimensional, continuous, or include disease states). A GP map is a (possibly stochastic) map $\varphi: G 	imes E 	o \mathcal{P}(P)$, where $\mathcal{P}(P)$ is the space of probability measures on $P$, that should incorporate:

1. Gene expression dynamics: an intermediate transcriptomic/proteomic layer $T$ with maps $G 	imes E 	o \mathcal{P}(T) 	o \mathcal{P}(P)$ encoding regulatory networks and gene–gene interactions (epistasis).
2. Omnigenic inheritance: the contribution to a typical complex phenotype is spread across a very large fraction of loci, so the map must remain well-defined and tractable when essentially all coordinates of $G$ contribute non-trivially to $\varphi$.
3. Evolutionary dynamics: a stochastic process $(G_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on $G$ combining deterministic selection driven by a fitness functional $F: \mathcal{P}(P) 	o \mathbb{R}$ pulled back through $\varphi$, together with stochastic effects (mutation, recombination, genetic drift in finite populations).

Problem: Construct such a class of GP maps $\varphi$, together with the associated evolutionary stochastic dynamics, satisfying the following properties:
(a) Identifiability/learnability from realistic genomic and phenotypic data.
(b) Predictive power for the distribution of complex phenotypes and disease risks given $G$ and $E$.
(c) Compatibility with omnigenic architectures (i.e., the model class does not collapse or become statistically vacuous when the number of contributing loci is comparable to the genome size).
(d) A rigorous limit theorem describing the long-time behavior of the induced phenotype distribution under the combined deterministic selection and stochastic mutation/drift dynamics.

Provide either an explicit construction meeting (a)–(d) or prove obstructions showing that no such GP map class can simultaneously satisfy them.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad foundational research direction in mathematical and evolutionary biology rather than a precisely formulated conjecture. No construction or impossibility result is known that simultaneously satisfies identifiability, predictive power for complex traits, compatibility with omnigenic architectures, and a rigorous limit theorem under combined deterministic and stochastic evolutionary dynamics; the question remains an active open problem.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
status_evidence.snippet: Lists genotype-to-phenotype mapping among unresolved problems requiring more sophisticated mathematical frameworks, especially under omnigenic inheritance.
status_evidence.claim: Posed as an open problem in a 2022 collection of open problems in mathematical biology.

status_evidence.title: An Expanded View of Complex Traits: From Polygenic to Omnigenic (Boyle, Li, Pritchard)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes that essentially all expressed genes contribute to complex traits, motivating new mathematical models of GP maps.
status_evidence.claim: The omnigenic hypothesis motivating this open problem is itself a recent and unresolved modeling challenge.
